problem: If the $16$th term of an arithmetic series is $-32$ and the sum of the first $20$ terms is $-200,$ then the first term of the series is ${a}_{1}=${{field-1}}.

feedback.problem: If the $6$th term of an arithmetic series is $\frac{37}{4}$ and the sum of the first $16$ terms is $228,$ then the first term of the series is ${a}_{1}=${{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
We are given one term of the series. So, to find the first term, we use the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series in the form

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{N}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(N-1)d),
$$

where ${a}_{1}$ is the first term, $d$ is the common difference, and $N$ is the number of terms.

Substituting $N=16$ and ${S}_{N}=228$ into the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{N}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(N-1)d) \\ 228 & =\frac{16}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(16-1)d) \\ 228 & =8(2{a}_{1}+15d) \\ \frac{57}{2} & =2{a}_{1}+15d.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, we can write an equation for the $6$th term of the arithmetic series and substitute in its known value:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)d \\ {a}_{6} & ={a}_{1}+(6-1)d \\ \frac{37}{4} & ={a}_{1}+5d\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we obtain the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}\frac{37}{4}={a}_{1}+5d \\ \frac{57}{2}=2{a}_{1}+15d\end{aligned}
$$

To solve this system, we multiply the first equation by $-2$ and add the result to the second equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{37}{2} & =-2{a}_{1}-10d \\ \frac{57}{2} & =2{a}_{1}+15d \\ \frac{20}{2} & =5d \\ d & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $d=2$ into the first equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{37}{4} & ={a}_{1}+5d \\ \frac{37}{4} & ={a}_{1}+5(2) \\ \frac{37}{4} & ={a}_{1}+\frac{40}{4} \\ {a}_{1} & =-\frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
